title: Block-model asset gallery
hypothesis: Deterministically generated blocky GLB placeholders, built from the Confluence bestiary briefs, read as their intended silhouettes at player-relative scale — making cheap side-by-side design iteration (including variants of the same creature) possible before any real art exists.
success_signals: All seven generated GLBs load through the asset registry without errors.
Each creature is recognizable as its bestiary brief from silhouette and color alone.
The two Mugosh design variants can be compared side by side against the reference capsule.
A broken GLB path falls back to the declared fallback asset instead of crashing.
kill_criteria: Blocky generation cannot express a brief's silhouette even after spec iteration (tool failure).
GLB loading is unreliable enough that the registry path cannot be trusted (pipeline failure).
reset_strategy: Destroy the gallery root entity and rebuild every pedestal by reloading each asset from the registry. No backend state involved.
